clue.text: Goldwyn, say, you are tops with seven on film

parts.note: Sam Goldwyn was the Hollywood producer, so his first name is wanted
in text-speak 'you are' is written U R
A1 means first-rate, the very best, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A tribute to a movie mogul who is the best when working alongside a cast of seven.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the Kurosawa film Seven Samurai: the warriors who appear with 'seven' in a film title.
explanation.definitionFit: Kurosawa's classic film is called Seven Samurai, so these Japanese warriors come with the number seven on screen.

clue.text: So short a time behind the winner

definitions.meaning: a tiny unit of time, often shortened to sec
runner-up, finishing in the place after first

explanation.surface: Someone only a moment behind the race winner.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sixtieth of a minute, a brief moment, and finishing as runner-up after first place.

clue.text: Cobbler goes round a winding course

indicators.note: one word goes round another, which sits inside it

parts.note: a cobbler mends shoes, so he is a mender

explanation.surface: A shoe-repairer takes a twisting route.
explanation.definitionFit: A meander is a loop or bend in a river, or any twisting route.

clue.text: Make overland dash ? That's not very bright

parts.note: to dash is to rush
to light is to alight, to come down on land after a journey

explanation.surface: Suggests a cross-country sprint by someone not very clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very bright' reads as dim-witted, but it describes a feeble candle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rushlight was a cheap candle made from a rush dipped in fat, giving a dim glow.

clue.text: Nobody's so 25 ac

definitions.meaning: read as 'no body', something that has no body or physical form
25 across is SPIRITUAL, meaning not material, of the spirit

explanation.surface: A terse remark that no one is like that.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bodiless or immaterial has no physical frame, which is what spirit-like means.

clue.text: High transport status of eldest son, it's said

indicators.note: signals that the words are spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the eldest son traditionally inherits, so his position is that of heir

explanation.surface: A note on the standing of a firstborn son, with a mention of lofty travel.
explanation.walkthrough: HEIRSHIP, the position of being heir, sounds like the answer when the H is dropped as it often is in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirigible or blimp is a lighter-than-air craft that carries people high above the ground.

clue.text: You've had it when it's up with you

definitions.text: You've had it when it's up with you

parts.words: You've had it when it's up with you
parts.note: the idiom 'it's ... up with you' means you are finished

explanation.surface: A warning that one's fate is sealed.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying that everything is up with someone means they are done for, so the missing word completes the idiom.

clue.text: To sum up, with deference to King in return

indicators.note: the letters are made to return, read back from end to start

parts.note: pace, from Latin, is used to mean with due respect to someone
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A summary offered politely to the monarch in exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' turns PACER round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to recapitulate, going back over the main points briefly.

clue.text: Girl was one rather careless in match-play

definitions.text: was one rather careless in match-play
definitions.meaning: in Struwwelpeter, the Dreadful Story of ... and the Matches tells of a girl who plays with matches and burns

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a young woman playing sloppily in a golf or tennis match.
explanation.walkthrough: Match-play suggests golf, but it is literal: Heinrich Hoffmann's cautionary tale has a girl who plays with matches.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's name, and the Struwwelpeter heroine of that name played carelessly with matches.

clue.text: Boy in housemaid's room ? Fault's academic

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: a pantry is a service room where provisions are kept
Ed is a boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A lad found in a servant's quarters, and a scholar's fault.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a little sentence: this fault is an academic one.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive concern with petty rules and fine detail is a scholarly failing.

clue.text: First-class state of such literature

parts.note: Greek and Roman writing is held up as the model of first-class work, and the adjective for it also means of the highest class

explanation.surface: A judgement on how fine a body of writing is.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the literature of ancient Greece and Rome and, more widely, anything of lasting first-rate quality.

clue.text: Was concerned about a stop order

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about
a red light orders traffic to stop

explanation.surface: Someone worried about an instruction to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been concerned is to have minded or worried, the past tense of feeling concern.

clue.text: Like Gordius's problem, it turned a boy on

indicators.note: the words are turned round so that the letters run backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A remark about a classical puzzle that excited a young man.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordius tied the Gordian knot, so his problem was knotted; the answer is the adjective from the Latin nodus, a knot.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodal means relating to a node or knot, and the Gordian knot was the famous tangle Alexander cut.

clue.text: How we get news by 23, though one wedding-guest missed it

definitions.meaning: 23 is radio; signal quality on a wireless set is what lets us hear the news
in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner the Wedding-Guest is detained by the Mariner and never reaches the wedding party

explanation.surface: A comment on hearing the news over the wireless, and on a guest who missed a wedding party.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both how well a broadcast signal is received and the party held after a wedding, which Coleridge's Wedding-Guest never got to.

clue.text: Last seen going down American rabbit-holes

definitions.text: Last seen going down American rabbit-holes

parts.words: Last seen going down American rabbit-holes
parts.note: the white fluffy rear ends of a common American rabbit are the last thing visible as it bolts down its burrow

explanation.surface: Sounds like a missing-person report about someone who vanished down a burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The cottontail is a North American rabbit named after its white scut, seen as it dives into its burrow.

clue.text: He foretells development of giant root crops

indicators.note: the letters undergo a development, being worked up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A forecaster predicts the growth of enormous vegetable harvests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development of' reworks the fourteen letters of 'giant root crops' into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecaster or seer is someone who predicts what is to come.

clue.text: Cause of multiple deaths, said Julius Caesar

definitions.text: Cause of multiple deaths, said Julius Caesar

parts.words: Cause of multiple deaths, said Julius Caesar
parts.note: Shakespeare's Caesar says those who lack courage die many times before their deaths

explanation.surface: Reads like an emperor's verdict on a massacre.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Julius Caesar says 'Cowards die many times before their deaths; The valiant never taste of death but once.'
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of courage, by Caesar's line, makes the faint-hearted die many times over.

clue.text: Breakfast crack a curate dared not make ?

definitions.text: Breakfast crack a curate dared not make

parts.words: Breakfast crack a curate dared not make
parts.note: in the Punch cartoon the timid curate, served a bad egg by his bishop, says it is good in parts; he dared not crack a joke about it

explanation.surface: A breakfast joke too risky for a junior clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'curate's egg', from an 1895 Punch cartoon, is something good in parts; crack here is both a quip and a split in the egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin outer casing of an egg is what gets cracked at breakfast.

clue.text: Provision for retirement where Gilpin's horse stopped

definitions.text: Provision for retirement where Gilpin's horse stopped

parts.words: Provision for retirement where Gilpin's horse stopped
parts.note: retirement means going to bed, and in Cowper's ballad John Gilpin's runaway horse finally halted at the Hertfordshire town of Ware

explanation.surface: Sounds like a pension scheme connected to a famous runaway horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here is going to bed, not leaving work. The famous oversized Elizabethan bed, now in the V&A, came from Ware, where Gilpin's horse stopped in Cowper's comic poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The huge carved Elizabethan bed from the town of Ware in Hertfordshire could sleep several couples at once.

clue.text: Terribly angered

indicators.note: the word is treated terribly, its letters thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone driven to fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges ANGERED into a word that also means terribly angered.
explanation.definitionFit: To be furious is to be very angry, exactly what the two clue words say.

clue.text: Defence work makes us have fresh misgivings

parts.note: re- is the prefix for again, afresh
doubts are misgivings

explanation.surface: A building project leaves people with new reservations.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a small fortification or stronghold.

clue.text: A type of suit for a tough old bird

definitions.meaning: a one-piece overall worn for dirty work
an older hen fit only for boiling, not roasting

explanation.surface: Picking the right outfit for a hardy elderly person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a one-piece work overall, and an old hen tough enough that it must be stewed.

clue.text: Source of tenant's seasonal booking

definitions.meaning: a small fountain or stream-head is where water rises
a let taken for the spring season, split into two words

explanation.surface: Looks like the origin of a lodger's holiday rental.
explanation.definitionFit: A springlet is a little spring, the head of a stream; split in two it is a rental for the springtime.

clue.text: Tender shark

definitions.meaning: to tend is to care for the sick
the ... shark is a bottom-dwelling species

explanation.surface: A gentle shark.
explanation.definitionFit: It means to care for, as one tends a patient, and is also a species of slow, bottom-feeding shark.

clue.text: Sound of the waves

parts.note: not the sea's roar but sound carried on the airwaves

explanation.surface: The noise of the sea breaking on the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasting sends sound over electromagnetic airwaves to wireless receivers.

clue.text: Poor Tom. First name for an unfinished poem

definitions.meaning: in King Lear Gloucester's son disguises himself as the mad beggar Poor Tom

definitions.text: First name for an unfinished poem
definitions.meaning: a poem cut short is POE

explanation.surface: A mention of a pitiable fellow, then a title for a work left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished poem' is POEM without its last letter, POE, the American writer whose first name is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloucester's son in King Lear goes disguised as Poor Tom, and the same forename belonged to the writer Poe.

clue.text: Song such lords might sing?

parts.note: the bishops in the House of Lords are the Lords ..., so their song would carry the same adjective

explanation.surface: Wondering what music members of the House of Lords would perform.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishops who sit in Britain's House of Lords are called the Lords Spiritual; the word is also a gospel song.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious folk song of African-American tradition shares its name with the bishops' title in the Lords.

clue.text: Note light in the sky

definitions.meaning: the fifth note of the ...-fa scale
The Latin name for the sun

explanation.surface: Spotting a light up in the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the fifth note of the tonic sol-fa scale and also the sun, named after the Roman sun god.

clue.text: Blue-gowned Miss?

parts.note: the real girl behind Alice in Wonderland, pictured in a blue dress, gave her name to the Alice blue shade

explanation.surface: A query about a young woman in a blue dress.
explanation.walkthrough: Alice Liddell was the girl for whom Lewis Carroll wrote Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, and Alice is drawn in a blue dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice, the real-life model for Carroll's heroine, is shown in a blue frock, so she is the blue-gowned young lady.

clue.text: The mountain sheep are (Peacock)

parts.note: the opening of Thomas Love Peacock's War-Song of Dinas Vawr, whose next word completes the quotation

explanation.surface: The start of a line of verse about hill sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: Peacock's line runs 'The mountain sheep are sweeter, But the valley sheep are fatter'; the scan prints a dash where the missing word goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Peacock's poem says the hill sheep taste better than the valley ones, and the missing comparative supplies that.
